title: Midnight by Todrick Hall #todrickhall #midnightmusical #broadwayrevie...
transcript: Extraordinary vocals, a sticky score, and a palpable energy make this new musical by Todrick Hall a must-see, and it's not even on Broadway yet. Todrick has long-standing roots in the theatre, but his claim to fame in the 2010s was his YouTube career where he created sketches, parodies, and music videos. This incredibly ambitious project takes every craft he's honed over the years as a visionary, performer, and writer, gloriously melded into something that's undeniably memorable, even if rough around the edges. In the era of slavery in the American South, a group of 12 people navigate the pressures and prejudices that the surrounding social structures have prescribed to them. At the center of this story are Rail and Richard, who find in each other a long lost brother, far more than their racial divide should allow. The plot is compelling enough, despite the heavy-handed messaging and the occasionally overstuffed book. You don't really have the mental capacity to critique this while you're experiencing the show, though. It's entirely sung-through, moves at an impressive clip, and consistently bombards you with big production numbers and truly astonishing vocal performances. It honestly feels like a Broadway production, just in an off-Broadway house. With the level of detail in the design elements, especially the costuming, as well as how full and polished the choreography and orchestrations are, I don't think it's a matter of if it'll transfer — it's a matter of when. I was also impressed by the sound mixing and pleasantly surprised that I could understand every word, considering how lyrically dense the score is. It's a lot, like everything else about this show. I think it's cohesive, but the maximalist approach won't be for everyone. When every song wallops you like a showstopper, it begins to dilute the storytelling. That said, I love a show that takes big swings, and I still think this is commercially viable. You can draw some parallels to Hamilton and The Color Purple, and there are some motifs in here, like shoes and clocks, that have already been beaten to death in the canon of musical theatre. What sets this one apart is the original story and the score — we absolutely need a cast recording. I'm really curious to see how this will be received, especially that unforgettably subversive choice in Act 2. I'm no crystal ball, but I think this show will deservedly be getting a lot of buzz in the near future, and I would get your tickets now.
reasoning: Reviewer calls it a must-see, predicts a Broadway transfer, praises vocals/design/score, and explicitly urges viewers to get tickets now. Caveats about maximalism and heavy-handed book are present but minor.
